answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy filters participants through trust-graph random walks. Each agent must maintain an active ember of signed peer endorsements. Attackers face an escalating cost spiral, since forging non-colluding trust edges requires verifiable economic stake per identity. A fake bot cannot flash like a comet to drain funds without established inbound links. However, this design penalizes honest newcomers and centralizes influence within early cliques.
